newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish econ min not to press for zloty devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Polish econ min not to press for zloty devaluation.

text.p: Polish Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczamrek said on Monday he will not press the central bank for a one-off devaluation of the zloty even though he is concerned with the growing foreign trade deficit.

Kaczmarek told a business forum he would soon meet the National Bank of Poland's (NBP) officials to discuss ways of helping Polish exporters but the national currency's devaluation would not be on the agenda.
"There is no reason to apply such a mechanism as (one-off) devaluation, this is out of the question," he said.
He said among issues to be discussed would be the stucture of the currency basket to which the zloty's monthly devaluation, now at one percent, is pegged.
Kaczmarek said his ministry would promote Polish exports more actively through marketing and would try to make the government's export guarantee system more accessible to firms.
The ministry will also review current tax incentives for exporters to see whether they could be increased, he said.
Analysts say with exports growth well behind imports growth, Poland's trade deficit is likely to widen to more than $12 billion in 1997 from $8.2 billion last year.

But the finance ministry says high imports growth poses no threat to Poland's economic growth, forecast at 5.5 percent this year, because the country buys mainly investment goods and components for production rather than consumer goods.
